binders: There exists a real constant c.
Universally quantify a finite index type ι, a measurable space Ω, a probability measure μ on Ω, and a family X:ι→Ω→Real.
Universally quantify a real threshold t.
hypotheses: For every i, X_i is measurable and admits a real K>0 for which exp(X_i²/K²) is integrable and has integral at most 2; the definition redundantly repeats measurability and K>0 inside the witness condition.
For every i, X_i is integrable and ∫X_i dμ=0.
The family (X_i) is mutually independent under μ.
conclusions: μ({ω:|Σ_i X_i(ω)|≥t}), converted to Real, is at most 2 exp(−c t²/Σ_i N_μ(X_i)²).
mathematical_definitions: N_μ(X) is the ENNReal infimum of all finite nonzero ENNReal s such that X is measurable, exp(X²/s.toReal²) is integrable, and its integral is at most 2; the bound uses N_μ(X).toReal.
LocalDef003 says X is measurable and has a positive real exponential-square witness K.
The event sum and denominator sum range over every element of the finite type ι.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a universal real c>0 such that, for every finite family of mutually independent, centered, integrable real random variables on any probability space, if each variable is measurable and has an exponential-square moment bounded by 2 at some positive scale, then for every t≥0 the probability that the absolute value of their sum is at least t is at most 2 exp(−c t² divided by the sum of the squared real-valued infimal exponential-square scales).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The same c must work uniformly over all finite index types, probability spaces, families, and thresholds.
The index type may be empty; no nonemptiness assumption is present.
The infimum scale may equal 0 even though every candidate scale is nonzero; the proposition does not assert a positive denominator.
If the denominator is 0, Lean's real division by zero yields 0, so the right side becomes 2 rather than an infinite-decay interpretation.

If the admissible-scale set were empty, its ENNReal infimum would be top and toReal(top)=0; under the stated witness hypothesis it is expected to be nonempty, but finiteness/nonemptiness is not separately asserted in the conclusion.
No identical-distribution, variance normalization, or bound on the number of variables is assumed.
The statement is conditional and imposes no conclusion on families failing any antecedent.
